narrative:
The model determined that you have a 28% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, your other installment plans, and the length of the loan you requested. Your credit history of critical or other existing credits was the single most important reason for the denial. This history pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk, as the bank sees applicants with this background as higher risk compared with the majority of approved applicants who have steadily paid existing loans on time.

The second most influential factor was that you have other installment plans with a bank. This detail worked against you by increasing the predicted risk, since most approved applicants have no such additional payment obligations.

Your requested loan duration of 12 months was the third most important driver. This shorter timeframe actually helped your case by pushing the prediction toward good credit, as approved loans average nearly 20 months. Unfortunately, these positive effects were not enough to overcome the concerns raised by your credit history and existing bank installments.

You should focus on clearing or refinancing your current installment plans and ensuring all future payments are made on time to build a stronger credit history. Once these areas improve, reapply for a loan.
